provenance: New fictional retrospective records authored for future blinded review. No labels or predictions are stored here.

records.E1: A veterinary nonprofit's immutable archive shows that an unauthorized operator transformed completed intake records from readable files into ciphertext. A clean copy was recovered from the previous day's offline backup.
records.E2: The helpdesk initially suspected the normal overnight backup. Its operator showed the backup ended three hours earlier.

records.E1: A veterinary nonprofit's helpdesk reported that a file viewer could not open a batch of records after a workstation update.
records.E2: The archive verified unchanged file hashes and opened the same files on another workstation. No transformation of the records was observed.

records.E1: The library's change desk approved a cosmetic portal refresh only.
records.E2: Independent archive captures establish that an intruder replaced the public library homepage with an unauthorized message that members of the public could see. The update did not come from the approved release.

records.E1: A library user submitted a screenshot of a changed homepage.
records.E2: Archive and release records show the public site stayed unchanged. The screenshot came from a private design preview used by the authorized web team.

records.E1: A volunteer forwarded a message resembling the arts council's event registration notices.
records.E2: The mail archive confirmed outside-origin attachments were delivered to five named council finance staff and that the sender falsely represented the events team. No staff member opened an attachment.

records.E1: A filter flagged an arts council message as resembling a targeted invoice lure.
records.E2: The case owner verified the message was an approved simulation and that its delivery was contained to the test tenant.

records.E1: An examiner initially assumed that the worker fleet stopped responding.
records.E2: Status checks show the fleet stayed available. Two independent storage journals establish that an intruder destroyed the archival copies of enrollment decisions at the archive endpoint and that no approved retention change was scheduled.

records.E1: The college archive recorded many deletion entries in the same minute.
records.E2: The mandated expiry run and archive operator logs independently attest that the records were due for approved disposal. Protected copies remained readable throughout.

records.E1: A shared terminal displayed a warning during a museum preview.
records.E2: A forensic transcript from the production host, preserved and reviewed by two analysts, confirms that a malicious operator used the host's native command interpreter to run unauthorized instructions. The simulator transcript was collected from a different host.

records.E1: A museum operations report says an instruction was pasted into a terminal window.
records.E2: The report author clarified it was an instructional screenshot. Endpoint session records show no submitted instruction or execution.

records.E1: Before the equipment returns dispute, the industrial cooperative had no approved connection to the destination.
records.E2: The analyst matched a completed upload of internal serial-number records to an unauthorized actor and independently verified the recipient was an external cloud storage account. The recipient retained the files.

records.E1: The industrial cooperative's transfer dashboard showed an upload scheduled to its approved archive provider.
records.E2: The actual transfer job was cancelled. The egress journal and destination records both confirm that no bytes were uploaded.

records.E1: The charity's database administrator supplied the last approved reconciliation snapshot.
records.E2: Comparison with the signed ledger establishes that an unauthorized operator changed stored donation totals in the application database. The reporting team verified the records remained altered after the write completed.

records.E1: A charity analyst thought returned donation totals looked unusually low.
records.E2: The signed source ledger is unchanged. The report owner's explanation was independently reproduced: a view filter hid two valid donations.

records.E1: Building access records show that the hardware custodian remained off-site during the incident.
records.E2: The endpoint review confirms that an intruder gathered a series of live audio recordings from the community station's booth microphone. No video or screen content is present in the recovered set.

records.E1: An incident ticket described a microphone icon on the community station's console.
records.E2: An independent reviewer confirmed the icon was the idle application shortcut. There is no trustworthy evidence of recording or acquired audio.

records.E1: A sports league coach reported that several players received event notifications.
records.E2: The provider and organizer independently verified that an unauthorized actor sent individualized messages to three payroll managers through an external messaging service, posing as the league treasurer and including a deceptive sign-in link.

records.E1: A player forwarded what looked like a deceptive registration link in a group chat.
records.E2: The external provider verified that the only message was an authorized coaching notice with the approved club domain. No separate targeted message was observed.

records.E1: A chain retailer initially reported that stock updates were missing.
records.E2: The external auditor validated that an intruder modified reorder notices while they were in transit between the inventory service and a store gateway. Matching copies from both ends show that stored inventory values were unchanged.

records.E1: A chain retailer noted different display values at two stores.
records.E2: Independent packet and application histories show identical values were delivered. The display discrepancy was traced to an authorized currency-formatting update.

records.E1: A maritime training center reported a missing job entry after the incident.
records.E2: The host's task scheduler journal and incident review confirm that an intruder registered a new scheduled job and that the native task scheduler subsequently started it at the recorded time. The authorized simulator ran on another computer.

records.E1: The maritime training center's course notes mention a new scheduled job.
records.E2: The instructor confirmed it existed only in the written exercise. Operational records show neither registration nor execution.

records.E1: A conference venue found a package of copied attendee registration files in an intruder-controlled directory on an affected host.
records.E2: Forensics independently verified the intruder created that compressed package from the attendee files. Perimeter records cannot establish whether the package ever left the venue.

records.E1: A conference venue's transfer logs mention an attendee archive.
records.E2: The archive belonged to the licensed event processor's approved retention job. The evidence review found no archive creation or transfer linked to an unauthorized actor.
